title: Clauses in the right order
prompt: Arrange the clauses into a query that returns each rack's average inlet temperature since noon, keeps only racks averaging above 26 °C, hottest first. One block doesn't belong in a valid query.
hints: SQL's written order is SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, even though the engine evaluates FROM first.
WHERE filters individual rows before grouping, so it can't use an aggregate like AVG. A condition on a group's aggregate belongs in HAVING.
The time condition is a WHERE (on rows); the average condition is a HAVING (on groups).
